mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with FEDFUNDS declining over 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals restrictive monetary policy that suppresses corporate borrowing and economic growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with FEDFUNDS above 5.0% for two consecutive months, or Rank IC remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in nonfarm payrolls signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with UNRATE declining and PAYEMS rising, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, a decline in residential construction permits below the 12-month moving average indicates weakening housing demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of late-cycle periods with HOUST below 12-month MA, or Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production over the prior 3 months indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate profit growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with INDPRO increasing over 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index rises above 3.5% year-over-year for three consecutive months, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with CPIAUCSL above 3.5% YoY for three consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regimes, a sharp decline in unemployment rate below 4.0% within one month indicates rapid labor market recovery that boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with UNRATE declining below 4.0% within one month during high-unemployment regimes, or Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production and nonfarm payrolls signals robust economic activity across manufacturing and labor markets, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with INDPRO and PAYEMS both increasing, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.02.
